questions.question: The melting point of a solid is defined as:

options.text: the minimum temperature at which the solid melts to become liquid at the atmospheric pressure
the minimum temperature at which the solid melts to become liquid at a high pressure
the minimum temperature at which the solid melts to become liquid at a low pressure
the maximum temperature at which the solid melts to become liquid at atmospheric pressure

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**the minimum temperature at which the solid melts to become liquid at the atmospheric pressure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **melting point** of a solid is a fundamental physical property.
 
• It is defined as the **temperature** at which the solid phase changes to the liquid phase at **atmospheric pressure**.
 
• This transition occurs because the **thermal energy** provided at the melting point is sufficient to overcome the **intermolecular forces** holding the solid together.
 
• The melting point is a characteristic property of a substance and can be used to **identify** and **purify** materials.
 
• For pure substances, the melting point is a **sharp** and distinct temperature, but for mixtures, it may vary over a range of temperatures.
 
• At the melting point, the solid and liquid phases are in **equilibrium**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **High Pressure**__

 __
 
• When we talk about melting points at **high pressure**, the melting point can change. However, the definition typically refers to atmospheric pressure, which is the standard condition.
 
 
 
• **Low Pressure**__
 __
 
• Similarly, melting points at **low pressure** are different and can vary from those at atmospheric pressure. This is because pressure affects the physical properties of substances.
 
 
 
• **Maximum Temperature**__
 
 
• The term **maximum temperature** is incorrect in the context of melting points because the melting point is a specific temperature, not a range or maximum value.

• The allocation of seats is based on the population of each state and union territory.
 
 
 
• **5th Schedule**__
 __

• It also provides for the establishment of **Tribes Advisory Councils** to advise on matters pertaining to the welfare and advancement of the Scheduled Tribes.
 
 
 
• **7th Schedule**__

• The Union List contains subjects on which only the Parliament can legislate, the State List contains subjects on which only the state legislatures can legislate, and the Concurrent List contains subjects on which both the Parliament and state legislatures can legislate.

• This provision reflects the principles of **natural justice** and aims to prevent any misuse of power by the authorities.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that no person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself?

__
 
• **Article 20** of the **Indian Constitution** provides protection in respect of conviction for offences.
 
• It ensures that **no person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself**.
 
• This is a fundamental right provided under Part III of the Constitution.
 
• Article 20 has three clauses:
 
 
• **Clause (1)**: No person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of the law in force at the time of the commission of the act charged as an offence.
 
• **Clause (2)**: No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.
 
• **Clause (3)**: No person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.
 
 
 
• This article is crucial as it safeguards the rights of individuals against arbitrary and unjust legal actions.
 
• The principle behind this provision is the preservation of human dignity and the prevention of self-incrimination.

• **Article 26**__

• It allows every religious denomination or any section to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes.
 
 
 
• **Article 24**__
 
 
• **Article 24** prohibits the **employment of children below the age of 14 years** in factories, mines or any other hazardous employment.

questions.question: Which of the following has universal acceptability in discharge of debt & payment obligations?

__
 
• **Legal tender money** is money that must be accepted if offered in payment of a debt.
 
• It is recognized by the **law of the land** as a valid form of payment.
 
• In most countries, the central bank or government issues **legal tender money**.
 
• Examples include **coins and banknotes** issued by a central authority.
 
• **Legal tender money** is backed by the government and is universally accepted within the country.
 
• It is essential for **economic stability and functioning** of the financial system.

 __

• Bonds pay periodic interest and return the principal at maturity.
 
• They are not universally accepted for payment of debts and obligations.
 
 
 
• **Houses**__
 __
 
• **Houses** are tangible assets and real estate properties.
 
• They can be used as collateral for loans but are not a form of money.

• The **Upper Paleolithic** stage is marked by the emergence of **blade tools** and dates from around **30,000 years ago** to **10,000 years ago**.
 
• The **Paleolithic Age** represents the longest phase of human history and is significant for the development of early human technology and culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lower Paleolithic**

 
 
• It is the earliest subdivision of the Paleolithic or Old Stone Age.
 
• Key sites: **Sohan Valley** and **Attirampakkam**.
 
 
 
• **Middle Paleolithic**
 
 
• Known for the development of **Levallois technique** for making tools.
 
• Key sites: **Bhimbetka** and **Didwana**.
 
 
 
• **Upper Paleolithic**
 
 
• Characterized by a diversity of stone tools.
 
• Key sites: **Belan Valley** and **Bagor**.

questions.question: Which of the following elements was NOT part of the Financial Sector Reforms under the Liberalisation Model?

options.text: Permission to set up private banks
Setting of new branches without RBI approval
Investment limit in foreign banks up to 74%
RBI’s role was enhanced to gain control over banks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RBI's role was enhanced to gain control over banks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The statement that **RBI's role was enhanced to gain control over banks** is not part of the Financial Sector Reforms under the Liberalisation Model.
 
• The **Financial Sector Reforms** were aimed at liberalizing the banking sector, increasing competition, and enhancing the efficiency of financial intermediaries.
 
• **Liberalisation** involved reducing the role of the government and allowing market forces to play a greater role in the economy.
 
• Reforms included measures like **allowing private banks** to be established, **permitting foreign investment** in banks, and **removing the need for RBI approval** for setting up new branches.
 
• These measures were intended to create a more dynamic and competitive banking sector, rather than enhancing the regulatory control of the RBI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Permission to set up private banks**__

 __
 
• As part of the **Financial Sector Reforms**, private entities were allowed to set up banks, which increased competition and efficiency in the banking sector.
 
 
 
• **Investment limit in foreign banks up to 74%**__
 __
 
• The reforms also included allowing higher **foreign direct investment (FDI)** limits in banking, which brought in capital and global best practices.
 
 
 
• **Setting of new branches without RBI approval**__
 
 
• The need for **RBI's approval** for setting up new bank branches was removed to facilitate easier expansion and reach of banks across the country.

questions.question: On the maternal side, the Mughals were descendants of ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Genghis Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On the **maternal side**, the Mughals were descendants of **Genghis Khan**.
 
• **Genghis Khan**, originally named **Temujin**, was the founder of the **Mongol Empire**, which became the largest contiguous empire in history.
 
• He was born in the year **1162** and established the Mongol Empire by uniting the **nomadic tribes** of Northeast Asia.
 
• The Mughal dynasty in India traced its lineage to him through their founder, **Babur**, whose mother was a descendant of Genghis Khan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tajuddin Yalduz**__

 __
 
• **Tajuddin Yalduz** was a ruler of the **Ghurid Empire** in the 13th century.
 
• He was not directly related to the Mughal lineage.
 
 
 
• **Timur**__
 __
 
• **Timur**, also known as **Tamerlane**, was a 14th-century conqueror and the founder of the **Timurid Empire** in Persia and Central Asia.
 
• On the paternal side, the Mughals were descendants of Timur.
 
 
 
• **Mohammad Ghori**__
 
 
• **Muhammad Ghori** was a ruler of the **Ghurid Empire** who invaded India in the late 12th century.
 
• He played a crucial role in establishing Islamic rule in the Indian subcontinent but was not directly related to the Mughal dynasty.
